questionsToConsider: Which parts of the product do you want rated separately in the grid?
Should you ask only users who have been active for a few weeks, so they have real experience to report?
What score counts as unhappy for your product, and should it trigger the obstacle questions?

guide.howToUseResponses: Group the written answers by the job people use the product for, because the same complaint means different things to a daily user and an occasional one. Treat obstacles marked as blocking as bugs to triage this week. Track the share of users who would be very disappointed to lose the product over time, and reply to everyone who left an email before you start building what they asked for.

Edit the ranking list so every item is something your team is genuinely weighing up for the roadmap.
Send the link inside the product or by email to active users, and add their plan or account type as a hidden field if you want to compare groups.

faqs.q: What questions should a product feedback survey ask?
faqs.a: Ask what people use the product for, how well it does that job, what gets in their way and what they would change. A recommendation score and a question about how disappointed they would be without it help you track the trend.

faqs.q: Should I ask users which feature to build next?
faqs.a: Ask what problem the feature would solve rather than taking the request as written. This survey asks for the last time the product got in the way, which usually points to the real need.

faqs.q: How often should I send a product feedback survey?
faqs.a: Every few months to the same group is enough to spot trends without tiring people out. Send it sooner after a big release.

blocks.title: Thanks for using the product. Five minutes of your honest opinion will shape what we build next.
In a sentence, what do you mainly use it for?
How often do you use it?
How does it do on each of these?
Overall, how well does it do the job you use it for?
What works best for you? What would you miss most if it disappeared?
Tell us about the last time it got in your way. What were you trying to do?
Does that stop you getting the work done, or just slow you down?
If you could change one thing about the product, what would it be?
Rank these by what you would like us to work on first.
